# Results -- Study 262 (Short-Interest) on the cross-sectional snapshot

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Recipe: join a
hardcoded short-interest snapshot (short % of float for ~60 US names, as-of
2024-12-31) with forward returns; sort the cross-section into a high-SI quantile
(most heavily shorted) and a low-SI quantile (least shorted); compare forward
returns. Pinned against a label-shuffle null, a bootstrap CI, a horizon sweep,
and a cost-adjusted net spread. **Survivorship + staleness biased**: the basket
is fixed survivors and the short-interest reading is a single static snapshot --
all results are upper bounds. As-of **2026-06-17**.*

## Data stamp

| Source | Window | Shape | Fingerprint |
|--------|--------|-------|-------------|
| Hardcoded short-interest snapshot (short % float, days-to-cover) | settlement ~2024-12-31 | 60 tickers x 2 cols | `7c363ac43257` |
| yfinance forward returns (1m/3m/6m/12m, cache-only) | from 2024-12-31 | ~60 tickers x 4 horizons | *(populated on `--fetch`)* |

The committed core ships **without** the yfinance cache, so the reproducible
headline below is the *frozen* fallback (mirrored in the notebooks' `R` dict).
A single static cross-section of 60 names is, by construction, a weak-evidence
design -- the numbers reflect that.

## Primary specification (high-SI minus low-SI, 3-month forward)

| Portfolio | Mean 3m forward return | n |
|-----------|------------------------|---|
| High-SI (most shorted, top quintile) | -1.85% | 12 |
| Low-SI (least shorted, bottom quintile) | +4.10% | 12 |
| **Spread (high - low)** | **-5.95%** | -- |

- Cross-sectional (Welch) **spread *t* = -0.74** -- nowhere near the *t >= 2*
  bar. NB: this is a *cross-sectional* t-stat on a single snapshot, **not** a
  time-series HAC *t*. One snapshot cannot produce a robust HAC result.
- **OLS slope** of forward return on standardized short interest:
  **-1.42% per +1 SD**, *t* = **-0.61**, R^2 = 0.006 -- essentially flat.
- **Label-shuffle null** (2000 permutations): two-sided **p = 0.47**.
- **Bootstrap 95% CI on the spread: [-21.4%, +9.6%]** -- straddles zero, with
  27% of resamples flipping sign.

The faint negative spread leans toward the Boehmer-Jones-Zhang "informed shorts
bleed" story, but the evidence here is statistically a coin flip.

## Horizon sweep -- the sign is not stable

| Horizon | Spread | t |
|---------|--------|---|
| 1m | -2.10% | -0.41 |
| 3m | -5.95% | -0.74 |
| 6m | +3.40% | +0.33 |
| 12m | -8.20% | -0.55 |

The sign flips between horizons and no horizon clears *|t| >= 2* -- the
signature of noise, not signal.

## Tradability -- the cheap edge is on the wrong side

A negative spread implies *shorting* the heavily shorted names -- exactly the
hard-to-borrow, high-fee, squeeze-prone leg.

| Item | 3-month |
|------|---------|
| Gross spread | -5.95% |
| Cost (2x round-trip @25bps + ~8%/yr borrow on short leg) | 2.10% |
| **Net spread** | **-3.85%** |

Borrow alone (~8%/yr is generous for a crowded short -- the worst names run
30-100%+/yr) eats roughly a third of any 3-month edge before slippage. And the
squeeze risk (GameStop-style) is precisely concentrated in this leg.

## Positive control -- the machinery finds a slope when planted

On the deterministic synthetic cross-section (`data.synthetic_panel`) the same
sort recovers the planted SI->return slope and reads ~zero on the null:

| Planted slope `si_beta` | Spread | t | Reading |
|------------------------|--------|---|---------|
| -0.04 (informed shorts) | -12.12% | -4.34 | engine sees it (bleed) |
| 0.00 (null) | -1.18% | -0.43 | engine reads ~zero |
| +0.04 (squeeze) | +9.77% | +3.50 | engine sees it (bounce) |

The engine is honest. The real snapshot simply has no robust signal.

## Verdict

- **Signal -- NONE.** Spread *t* = -0.74 on the real snapshot; OLS slope *t* =
  -0.61; label-shuffle p = 0.47; bootstrap CI straddles zero; the sign flips
  across horizons. A single 60-name cross-section cannot deliver the robust
  HAC *t* >= 2 the desk requires, and the two literatures (informed-shorts vs
  squeeze) partially cancel. Literature support exists on both sides, which is
  the opposite of a clean signal. Verdict: **NONE**.
- **Tradability -- MIRAGE.** The only directional read (short the crowded names)
  lands on the most expensive, most dangerous leg: ~8%/yr+ borrow, wide spreads,
  and acute squeeze risk turn a faint, insignificant gross edge into a negative
  net one. Verdict: **MIRAGE**.
- **Survivorship + staleness -- named.** Fixed surviving basket plus a single
  static short-interest reading; all results are upper bounds on any live effect.
